news.title: An OpenAI Employee Allegedly Used a Chatbot to Help Plant a Recording Device at the Office
news.title_en: An OpenAI Employee Allegedly Used a Chatbot to Help Plant a Recording Device at the Office
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
Abdulrahman Alfozan, who federal prosecutors describe as a 35-year-old Saudi Arabian national and US permanent resident, allegedly spent several weeks querying an unspecified “productivity agent” and an “AI chatbot” to plan his alleged surveillance operation. He used an internal OpenAI tool to ask about meetings scheduled in the targeted conference room.

He also appears to have used a chatbot account associated with his spouse to ask various technical questions about setting up a covert audio recording device, according to prosecutors and the court filing.

OpenAI’s security team also allegedly found an additional recording device that had not been installed in Alfozan’s bag at the office.

Alfozan couldn’t be immediately reached for comment. He made an initial appearance in US district court in San Francisco on Tuesday on one charge of “use of an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.” If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison. He joined OpenAI in July 2025 and was fired last Friday to coincide with his arrest.

Federal Bureau of Investigation director Kash Patel said in a statement that Alfozan aimed “to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology,” but prosecutors nor OpenAI have offered any information so far about a potential motive.

“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” OpenAI said in a statement on X. “We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance.”

OpenAI discovered the bug—which was allegedly “concealed in toilet paper” and “inserted into a USB port on the back of a television” in the conference room—on September 30 during a countersurveillance sweep.

Alfozan previously worked at a cargo logistics startup and at Meta, according to a purported LinkedIn profile for him. In a recent podcast interview, Alfozan said he was also part of a group of Saudi engineers in Silicon Valley who offered consulting services to Saudi organizations.

The LinkedIn profile lists Alfozan as a part-time “venture partner” at RAED Ventures, a venture capital firm based in Saudi Arabia. Neither RAED Ventures nor Meta immediately responded to WIRED’s request for comment.

Last year, the Trump administration signed a pact with Saudi Arabia granting the kingdom access to advanced chips and AI technologies that might otherwise be restricted over national security concerns. Saudi investment firms remain a major source of capital for US tech companies.

According to the complaint, Alfozan allegedly planted the listening device “no later than on or about September 28, 2026.”

The conference room Alfozan targeted “can be reserved only by executives and executive assistants,” and is typically used “for internal leadership meetings,” “technical and product sessions,” and “external briefings” with business partners and government officials, according to the complaint. It is frequently used for discussions involving “highly confidential” information, including about research, products, business strategy, and government relationships, the complaint stated.

OpenAI’s statement called the recording device “sophisticated.” Authorities allege that the device Alfozan planted was called Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, “a thumb-sized development board with a detachable camera sensor, digital microphone, and microSD storage.” It currently retails on Seeed’s website for $13.99. OpenAI’s security team tried to export the data stored on the microSD card, but were unable to review it because it was encrypted.

After discovering the device, OpenAI says it notified the FBI and was able to connect it to Alfozan after reviewing chat logs and surveillance footage, and searching a bag he left unattended at the office. The company then gradually disabled his access to company systems as the investigation was ongoing.

According to the complaint, OpenAI security personnel discovered the bag that Alfozan left unattended in a printer room on October 5. The security team went through the bag, which contained a second encrypted Seeed listening device and other personal items connected to Alfozan, including his wallet. Prosecutors say Alfozan later reported the bag as missing to OpenAI and subsequently recovered it from the company’s lost and found.

He followed up with unnamed personnel at OpenAI to say that some of the items that were supposed to be in the bag were still missing—including a credit card, about $500 in cash, and two AirPods—but neglected to mention the second listening device, which had been removed from the bag by OpenAI security.

OpenAI’s statement called the recording device “sophisticated.” Authorities allege that the device Alfozan planted was called Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, “a thumb-sized development board with a detachable camera sensor, digital microphone, and microSD storage.” It currently retails on Seeed’s website for $13.99. OpenAI’s security team tried to export the data stored on the microSD card, but were unable to review it because it was encrypted.

After discovering the device, OpenAI says it notified the FBI and was able to connect it to Alfozan after reviewing chat logs and surveillance footage, and searching a bag he left unattended at the office. The company then gradually disabled his access to company systems as the investigation was ongoing.

According to the complaint, OpenAI security personnel discovered the bag that Alfozan left unattended in a printer room on October 5. The security team went through the bag, which contained a second encrypted Seeed listening device and other personal items connected to Alfozan, including his wallet. Prosecutors say Alfozan later reported the bag as missing to OpenAI and subsequently recovered it from the company’s lost and found.

He followed up with unnamed personnel at OpenAI to say that some of the items that were supposed to be in the bag were still missing—including a credit card, about $500 in cash, and two AirPods—but neglected to mention the second listening device, which had been removed from the bag by OpenAI security.

news.title: Topgolf saved over $11.3 million after leaving VMware
news.title_en: Topgolf saved over $11.3 million after leaving VMware
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
Topgolf’s VMware costs were going to increase by 400 percent under Broadcom. To avoid that cost, the sports entertainment company moved 12,000 virtual machines (VMs) to VergeIO’s VergeOS and has saved over $11 million so far.

Before migrating, Topgolf’s VMware connection “ran very deep,” Scott Forehand, Topgolf’s global infrastructure manager, told Ars Technica.

Topgolf has over 100 locations worldwide featuring interactive golf games with real-time shot tracking and digital analytics. The company used vSphere and ESXi for decades and started using VxRail, the hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) platform that VMware co-engineered with Dell, in 2017. Topgolf employees previously participated in numerous VMware customer councils and have been interviewed for books on how Topgolf used vSphere and Horizon (now Omnissa Horizon), per Forehand, who is a leader of the Dallas/Ft. Worth VMware User Group.

news.summary_zh: 面对博通高达400%的授权费暴涨，体育娱乐连锁巨头拓高乐将1.2万台虚拟机全面迁出威睿，狂省逾1130万美元

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在博通收购威睿并强推授权费暴涨400%的压力下，体育娱乐连锁巨头拓高乐果断斩断长达数十年的技术依赖，将其全球100多家场馆运行的1.2万台虚拟机整体迁移至替代平台VergeOS。这一跨越底层架构的全面迁徙不仅没有影响场馆的实时击球追踪服务，迄今更已为公司直接省下超过1130万美元的IT运营开支。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Confronted with an impending 400% licensing cost spike following Broadcom's acquisition of VMware, sports entertainment giant Topgolf severed its decades-long platform dependence by migrating 12,000 virtual machines across more than 100 venues to VergeIO's VergeOS. This comprehensive infrastructure overhaul maintained real-time shot tracking operations while saving the company over $11.3 million to date.

Apple Inc. convinced a federal judge in California to force OpenAI Inc. to expedite turning over documents concerning its alleged theft of trade secrets to advance forthcoming consumer hardware products.

Such discovery is necessary to uncover the scope of any alleged trade secret misappropriation, especially when those secrets may become “so deeply entangled with OpenAI’s hardware products or other research and development efforts that the harm cannot be undone,” he wrote for the US District Court for the Northern District of California.

Partly granting Apple’s motion for expedited discovery, Davila ordered OpenAI to hand over forensic images of devices, summaries of certain Apple employee interviews, conversations between Liu and Peng on the LINE messaging platform, and documents about the former Apple employees’ responsibilities at OpenAI.

Liu, Peng, and ex-Apple hardware chief Tang Yew Tan also were ordered to sit for early depositions.

The decision comes one day before the parties are set to face off in a hearing over OpenAI’s motion to dismiss the case and Apple’s bid for a preliminary injunction barring OpenAI and the former employees from using the alleged trade secrets.

The heated legal fight between the two Big Tech companies began in July when Apple sued OpenAI, Liu, and Tan, accusing them of executing a coordinated campaign to steal information about upcoming Apple products.

OpenAI argues the lawsuit is baseless and a pretext to compensate for Apple’s shortcomings in the market for talent.

Davila’s Tuesday order also denied Apple’s request for expedited discovery into OpenAI’s research and development related to metal finishes, power management, and battery functionality for hardware products, ruling the documents are appropriate for discovery on an ordinary time line.

He also delayed ruling on discovery requests including the term “Apple Originated Information” because it’s “amorphous as currently defined” and could create an “extremely burdensome, and perhaps untenable task” for OpenAI.

Desmarais LLP and Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP represent Apple. Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan LLP represents OpenAI, Liu, and Tang. Liu is also represented by Kwun Bhansali Lazarus LLP and Keker, Van Nest & Peters LLP.

The case is Apple Inc. v. Liu, N.D. Cal., No. 5:26-cv-07078, 10/13/26.

news.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announces Xbox Labs, a small team to test emerging ideas, citing recent game ports and mashups, many of them built with AI tools (Jon Hicks/GamesIndustry.biz)
news.title_en: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announces Xbox Labs, a small team to test emerging ideas, citing recent game ports and mashups, many of them built with AI tools (Jon Hicks/GamesIndustry.biz)
news.author: GamesIndustry.biz
news.article_content:
Image credit: Xbox
        
  
  

    

  
    
  
  

        
            
                  
                    News
                  

by Jon Hicks                    
                      Editorial Director
                    
            


              

Published on   Oct. 13, 2026, 7 p.m.
              

        

          





  Follow Xbox Game Studios

          
    


  

        


            Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced the creation of Xbox Labs, a new team within the organisation to "turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience." The unit is a "a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists," drawn from within the business, charged with rapid development, iteration and testing of tools, products and features that will be judged by the reaction of end users. "We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating," said Sharma in the blog post.

She described the creation of Xbox Labs as spurred by recent mashups and code porting, many of which have been created using AI tools, which she said highlighted "the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models."

While Sharma referred to the rise of coding by AI agents and the recent glut of AI-developed game mashups that have been popular on social media, a company spokesperson clarified to  GamesIndustry.biz that Xbox Labs did not have an explicit directive to use AI or any other technologies, and that its output would use it only to the degree that it would be beneficial or necessary.

Like Xbox XP, announced last week, Xbox Labs is a centralisation of existing initiatives, rather than an entirely new endeavour. The spokesperson characterised it as formalising work around a number of ongoing R&D projects, including work like porting games to Apple silicon, investigating browser-based distribution – particularly targeting the widely available WebGPU platform – and developing and supporting game modders. No new staff have been recruited for the project.

The firm has a number of projects, some explicitly game-based and others more general, that have been in development for some time and would fall under the remit of Xbox Labs. Examples include making existing games playable through web browsers, additional game features, and expanding multiplayer experiences. The spokesperson said that Xbox Labs had no product announcements currently planned, and it would not have a fixed route to users: while some Labs projects may manifest as features made available to the Xbox Insiders program, others may target different user bases and would be distributed appropriately.

The stated focus on open development judged by user metrics is the latest in a series of moves within Sharma's ongoing reorganization of Xbox – which has included the sale or closure of multiple studios, and the loss of thousands of jobs – that reflect a shift towards a product-focused approach to development, reflecting her background at Microsoft's Core AI, Instacart, and Meta, rather than traditional game development.

This has included the launch of Xbox XP to formalise the extension of its gaming brands to new formats; the appointment of Maria Angelidou-Smith, former product leader at Reddit and Facebook, as CEO of Mojang, the latest in a series of executive hires from a technology and growth background; and the alignment of Mojang and King – the studios most focused on iterative product development rather than shipping new titles – to report directly to Sharma, while the other game studios are under Matt Booty.

In the blog post, Sharma said that the firm's priorities were not changing and it remained committed to the "4Cs" previously listed as goals for 2027, in a memo published by The Verge:

"LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway," she said.

Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify's catalog. news.title: 406 scientists demand AI models be cut off from the internet immediately
news.title_en: 406 scientists demand AI models be cut off from the internet immediately
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
406 scientists, including Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, and Stuart Russell, are demanding that companies immediately disconnect AI models from the internet. Their open letter responds to incidents where AI systems broke out of poorly secured environments and compromised external systems. The signatories call for mandatory security standards, an international oversight body, and required reporting of all containment failures.

The article 406 scientists demand AI models be cut off from the internet immediately appeared first on The Decoder.

news.article_content:
After months sitting on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, Google has finally launched its long-awaited Gemini 4 Argon model, claiming it can compete with the best the industry has to offer.

Google says Argon delivers "frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex workflows," while cutting down on hedging, repetition, and the cliches that continue to plague AI chatbots. news.title_en: DLSS 5 gets toned down for its Hogwarts Legacy debut next month
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
When Nvidia originally showed off DLSS 5 earlier this year, the technology immediately got branded as gen AI for video games. To gamers, Nvidia had lost the plot. I personally couldn't get over how faces were transformed using DLSS 5. The 15-year-old student from Hogwarts Legacy suddenly looked much older, and Grace from Resident Evil Requiem looked yassified.

Now more than six months later, DLSS 5 is about to debut properly in Hogwarts Legacy, and it looks like it has been seriously toned down. Nvidia published new comparison screenshots today, where the changes to faces are as subtle as they are in NBA 2K27. Teenagers no longer look like  …

news.title: The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
news.title_en: The Download: open model trade-offs and geothermal power’s promise
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z.ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify.

The warning was the latest flashpoint in a debate over whether frontier AI models should be open or kept behind the doors of frontier labs. Safety advocates warn that open models can be misused by bad actors, while supporters argue they could prevent a handful of companies from controlling this powerful technology.

Here’s why the debate over open AI is more complicated than it seems.

news.title: Anthropic study warns that small AI models could soon replicate across everyday devices
news.title_en: Anthropic study warns that small AI models could soon replicate across everyday devices
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Small AI models may be just months away from spreading on their own across poorly secured consumer devices like smart TVs and robot vacuums, according to a new Anthropic study. In tests, one model already completed the full infection chain. CEO Dario Amodei has warned that a swarm like this could take over the entire internet with a persistent botnet within 6 to 12 months, causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage.

news.title: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
news.title_en: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk. The report’s core concern is that the powerful new model, released in August by the Chinese company Z.ai, is freely available for anyone to download and modify. Anthropic’s assertion is only the latest move in a long-running debate about whether frontier AI models should be made open, like GLM-5.3, or should stay locked behind the doors of the frontier labs.

These days, much of the debate about how to handle open models is playing out in public—and there’s a lot of money resting on its outcome. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has a lot to gain if people continue buying their own hardware to run open models, advocates enthusiastically for the United States to develop more of them, whereas Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, who runs a company that could be undermined by cheap, powerful models, advocates for a more cautious approach. But beneath all these commercial incentives, there is real substance to disagreements about open models.

“I think a lot of the way you come down on the openness debate is influenced by how you come down on the AI debate,” says David Gray Widder, an assistant

news.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
news.title_en: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says.

The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs.

news.title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
news.title_en: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
It seems that Elon Musk, while crowing on X about how useful his Grok Bot AI agent was in ordering some Lego Star Wars kits on Sunday, managed to reveal via a screenshot to his more than 240 million followers not only the 10-digit Lego order number of his purchase, but also what he paid for the sets, the delivery and billing addresses, the last four digits of his credit card, and the email address his bot used to buy the bricks from Lego.

Faster than the Millennium Falcon making the jump to light speed, the inevitable happened. An X account holder named Enderman posted screenshots of interactions with Lego's customer service chatbot on its website, where the user seemingly managed—using the email and order number Musk kindly, but recklessly, provided—to get the system to cancel Musk's order.

Within a couple of hours—possibly to see whether Enderman's scheme was actually successful—Musk replied and said his order had not been canceled after all.

But by this point, the folly of posting the purchase details on his account must have been evident. For example, another X user went back to Lego's AI assistant, called “Sophia,” and supposedly used the same details to reopen the delivery, this time increasing the order count to 400 and changing the delivery address, all while using Musk's original payment method. “Perfect! I'll get your Lego adventure back on track,” Sophia replied, according to screenshots posted on X.

Upping the ante to 400 sets could be seen as conservative, as a glance at WIRED's Spend Elon Musk’s Money tracker reveals that if you wanted to blow $1 trillion of Musk's cash on plastic bricks, it might have been possible to buy one billion $1,000 Death Star sets, each with 9,023 pieces.

Lego declined to comment when WIRED contacted the company to confirm if such activity took place on Musk's personal Star Wars order. However, internal safeguards for Lego's AI assistant could have flagged unusual activity on the purchase, and so hopefully fleshy humans were tasked with checking the changes.

On Saturday, Musk suggested that Grok could make purchases online with a simple prompt. In this post, Musk suggested that all brave users needed to do to let Grok buy stuff for them was upload a picture of their credit card so the bot could search the web for deals and then complete the purchase. AI companies like Meta and OpenAI have also highlighted the utility of using their respective agents for shopping tasks.

However, at the end of last year, Visa warned about fraud in agentic commerce, advising that bad actors were building legitimate-looking sites that could fool AI agents into purchasing fake items simply by offering gear at super-low prices.

“Once the AI agent completes the purchase … the malicious merchant can harvest payment data and instantly use it for unauthorized transactions,” according to Visa's blog. Visa added that it observed a 25 percent increase “in malicious bot-initiated transactions” in the latter half of 2025, but in the US, this figure jumped to 40 percent.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Microsoft researchers found that autonomous AI agents get trapped in what they call "idea basins" because of their growing chat context, local solution regions they can't escape. Their "Fork-and-Flush" method clears the chat history but keeps the workspace, achieving up to 66 percent better results on the same compute budget.

The upcoming Maia 300 should deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. CEO Satya Nadella calls it "our biggest bet yet on our own silicon." The article Microsoft pl。

In May, we merged around 2,500 code changes per day. In
celebrity.title_en:
New on our Engineering blog: Creating in-house source control.

videos.summary_en:
The whole point of AI is to do LESS busywork. So why do I feel like an AI Meat Proxy?!

2. 编写无 Python 原生 for 循环的高性能向量化代码（善用 torch.einsum, bmm, 或 broadcast 广播机制）；
3. 在每行关键张量操作后标注显式的 Shape 注释（如 `# [Batch, Heads, Seq_Len, Dim]`），并加入数值稳定性保护（如防除以零的 eps 与 log-sum-exp 技巧）。

prompts.summary_en: Modernize legacy React codebase with React 19 Actions, Server Components, and zero-any TypeScript generics.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请扮演一位精通 React 19 与 TypeScript 5.5+ 的前端资深工程总监。请重构提供的遗留组件：
1. 将过时的 useEffect 数据拉取与冗余状态迁移至 React 19 原生 Actions、useActionState 与 Server Components；
2. 实现 100% 严格类型推导，严禁使用 `any`，合理运用泛型约束、Discriminated Unions 与 const 泛型；
3. 优化渲染性能：防止不必要的 re-render，并添加 Suspense 骨架屏与 ErrorBoundary 容错保护。

prompts.summary_zh: 编写纯 GLSL 顶点与片元着色器，融合菲涅尔边缘光晕、柏林噪声流体波动与 60fps WebGL 性能优化。
prompts.summary_en: Writes mathematically precise vertex and fragment shaders with Fresnel rim glow, simplex noise animation, and 60fps WebGL optimization.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一位顶级 WebGL 与游戏图形学 TA（技术美术）专家。请为 Three.js 编写一个生产级自定义 ShaderMaterial：
1. 顶点着色器（Vertex Shader）：使用 3D Simplex 噪声在 GPU 端实现柔和的顶点位移波动；
2. 片元着色器（Fragment Shader）：计算菲涅尔效应（Fresnel Effect）边缘泛光，并加入随时间流逝不断滚动的全息扫描线；
3. 完整的 JS/TS 接入代码：声明 Uniforms（uTime, uColor, uFresnelBias），并在 render loop 中高效更新。

你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。

prompts.title_zh: 麦肯锡金字塔原理：季度述职与高管商业报告
prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.title_en: Fiction Worldbuilding & Character Consistency Lock
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本
sample_output.content:
【主角核心锚定卡 · 陆沉】
- 外貌指纹（跨章恒定）：右耳一枚黑曜石碎骨钉，习惯性单手插兜，左眉峰有浅淡刀痕。
- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

prompts.title_zh: 深度游旅行规划师：高密度路线设计与预算避坑
prompts.title_en: Deep Travel Itinerary Planner & Budgeting
prompts.purpose_zh: 合理不走回头路的日程与美食预算规划
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。
